notes: Three-shaped signs (m, ẖ, s) not separable by shape here; marked s? or m? by tail length. 'asor[.]yi': hatched sign between r and y read as lost (context soreyi suggests e). l.2 'woni': n is the rising stroke + 3 + long tail (could be read s + n). l.6 se? : cup with one stroke plus a pair of short strokes; the heavy stroke under the line number 6 read o; alternatively '(6)y se' or 'yse'. 'mñk?': crossed loop sign (ñ) sits on the long tail of a heavily inked sign read k?. 'te' = slash + hooked sign with long bar. 'to' = cup with dot. l.7: hatched sign with r-like strokes inside read r?; three small flat-topped signs read l l and then i. l.10: the sign under number 10 (hook top, long stroke, hatched foot) is unidentified, written [.]. 'd' = rising stroke with hook. ll.13-15 (added): r? = cup + hatched w-shaped part; three small signs 'b ñ? d?' before 'to' are v-shaped/crossed and uncertain; a small mark stands under the hatched r at line 15. The two-sign groups '/3' (slash left of 3) are ambiguous between q and s+o; here read s+o in asor- and q nowhere.

notes: Lines 3-4: a dotted stretch of about six dots before 'i?ii' (dots scattered, count approximate); the sign under number 4 is hatched with a long tail (k?). ḫ? = an L-shaped open sign (not the clear c-form ḫ seen in l.15-16); could be another value. d? = a 2/hook-shaped sign. q? = slash tightly joined to 3 (could be s + o) in ll. 11, 12, 17. to? in l.9 = an open cup without dot. Line 5-11 row ends without divider before line 12 (written with a space). In 'terikeeeb?kwi' the v-shaped sign b? stands on the long tail of k. Position of number 6 is between r and the following e; placed before r. 3-shaped signs (m, ẖ, s) are marked s?.

reading: w?[.]si : soreyi?(2)tei?eylowik?e b? : ẖ?lḫs?l?(3)teii : arikeep?lḫ? (4)os?n? : s?ḫe o : y?ib?[.][.][.][.]k(5)te : a(6)ḫm (7)yin?oke(8)te
notes: Faint, thin copy. l.1: first sign looks like a heavy w (б) read w?; the next sign is cross-hatched (o lost). The i of soreyi is an uncertain small hooked sign. i? after te (l.2) = an L-shape with a tick. y here is one long and two short strokes. k? in l.2 is hatched with a long tail. l.3/4: '52' at the row's right end read a; 'p?' = 2-shaped sign with long tail; n? = a rising stroke with a flat stroke (n in reduced form?) also in l.7; a dot stands under the s? after o in l.4. y? before i in l.5 = two strokes crossed by the bar of i. Four dots after b? = lost signs. The number 7 is faint (a tick over the strokes of y). No divider at the end of l.8. Line 3 ends 'teii' (two i's).
